campos.description: The Chants of Bewildering is a form of music used for entertainment originating in The Glad Bust.  The form guides musicians during improvised performances.  A chanter recites nonsensical words and sounds.  The entire performance is to be very loud.  The melody has short phrases throughout the form.  Only one pitch is ever played at a time.  It is performed using the anam scale.  Throughout, when possible, performers are to use mordents.  [B]The chanter always does the main melody and should feel mysterious.  [B]The Chants of Bewildering has a well-defined multi-passage structure: a passage, a bridge-passage and a lengthy finale.  [B]The simple passage is very fast.  The chanter's voice stays in the high register.  The passage is performed in free rhythm.  [B]The bridge-passage is at a free tempo.  The chanter's voice stays in the middle register.  The passage is performed in the uvel rhythm.  The passage should be performed using rapid runs.  [B]The finale is consistently slowing.  The chanter's voice ranges from the middle register to the high register.  The passage is performed in the ngárak rhythm.  [B]Scales are constructed from twelve notes dividing the octave.  In quartertones, their spacing is roughly 1-x-x-x-x--x-xx-x-x-x--xO, where 1 is the tonic, O marks the octave and x marks other notes.  The tonic note is fixed only at the time of performance.  Every note is named.  The names are ustos (spoken us), emär (em), izeg (iz), bemòng (be), gost (go), öntak (önt), tosid (to), feb (fe), ibruk (ib), ermis (erm), thoth (tho) and thatthil (tha).  [B]The anam hexatonic scale is constructed by selection of degrees from the fundamental scale.  The degrees selected are the 1st, the 3rd, the 5th, the 7th, the 9th and the 11th.  [B]The uvel rhythm is made from two patterns: the emuth (considered the primary) and the gòstang.  The patterns are to be played over the same period of time, concluding together regardless of beat number.  [B]The emuth rhythm is a single line with two beats.  The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| x x | [B]where x is a beat and | indicates a bar.  [B]The gòstang rhythm is a single line with four beats.  The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| - x - - | [B]where x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar.  [B]The ngárak rhythm is made from two patterns: the fer and the gòstang.  The patterns are to be played in the same beat, allowing one to repeat before the other is concluded.  [B]The fer rhythm is a single line with two beats.  The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| - x | [B]where x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar.

The Embraced Drums is a form of music used during marches and military engagements originating in The Glad Bust.  The rules of the form are applied by composers to produce individual pieces of music which can be performed.  Two chanters recite nonsensical words and sounds while the music is played on a mengmad, a kesham and a mothram.  The musical voices join in melody and counterpoint, harmony and rhythm.  The entire performance is moderately fast.  The melody and counterpoint both have mid-length phrases throughout the form.  Chords, seldom-used, are sparse -- intervals and single pitches are favored.  It is performed without preference for a scale and in free rhythm.  Throughout, when possible, composers and performers are to locally improvise and alternate tension and repose.  [B]Each chanter always should perform sweetly.  [B]The mengmad always should be jumpy and uses mordents.  [B]The kesham always should feel agitated.  [B]The mothram always should perform with skill.  [B]The Embraced Drums has a well-defined multi-passage structure: a first theme, a lengthy exposition of the first theme, a bridge-passage, a lengthy second theme, an exposition of the second theme, a bridge-passage and a synthesis of previous passages.  [B]The first theme is voiced by the melody of the mengmad, the counterpoint of the kesham, the harmony of the mothram and the rhythm of the chanters reciting nonsensical words and sounds.  The passage is to be loud.  The mengmad stays in the harsh high register and each of the chanters' voices ranges from the low register to the middle register.  [B]The first exposition is voiced by the melody of the mothram, the counterpoint of the kesham and the harmony of the mengmad.  The passage is to be soft.  The mengmad stays in the harsh high register.  [B]The first bridge-passage is voiced by the melody of the chanters reciting a composition of The Prim Books and the harmony of the mothram.  The passage is to become softer and softer.  Each of the chanters' voices stays in the high register.  [B]The second theme is voiced by the melody of the kesham, the counterpoint of the chanters reciting The Lizard of Dales and the rhythm of the mothram.  The passage is to become softer and softer.  Each of the chanters' voices ranges from the low register to the middle register.  [B]The second exposition is voiced by the melody of the mengmad, the melody of the mothram, the counterpoint of the chanters reciting The Lizard of Dales and the harmony of the kesham.  The passage is to be very loud.  The mengmad stays in the heavy low register and each of the chanters' voices covers its entire range.  [B]The second bridge-passage is voiced by the melody of the kesham, the harmony of the chanters reciting nonsensical words and sounds and the rhythm of the mengmad.  The passage is to be soft.  Each of the chanters' voices covers its entire range and the mengmad stays in the harsh high register.  [B]The synthesis is voiced by the melody of the kesham, the counterpoint of the mengmad and the rhythm of the mothram.  The passage is to fade into silence.  The mengmad stays in the harsh high register.

The Glitter of Poets is a devotional form of music originating in The Poison of Typhoons.  The form guides musicians during improvised performances.  A singer recites a composition of The Lyrical Wise Poetry.  The melody has short phrases throughout the form.  Only one pitch is ever played at a time.  It is performed using the ngub scale and in free rhythm.  Throughout, when possible, performers are to glide from note to note, use mordents, play rapid runs, play legato and match notes and syllables.  [B]The singer always does the main melody and should be spirited.  The voice stays in the middle register.  [B]The Glitter of Poets has a simple structure: three unrelated passages.  [B]Each of the simple passages is extremely fast, and it is to start loud then be immediately soft.  [B]Scales are constructed from twenty-four notes spaced evenly throughout the octave.  The tonic note is a fixed tone passed from teacher to student.  [B]The ngub heptatonic scale is constructed by selection of degrees from the fundamental scale.  The degrees selected are the 1st, the 4th, the 7th, the 10th, the 14th, the 17th and the 20th.

The Meadow of Playing is a form of music used during marches and military engagements originating in The Poison of Typhoons.  The form guides musicians during improvised performances.  Three chanters recite nonsensical words and sounds.  The melody has short phrases throughout the form.  Only one pitch is ever played at a time.  The music repeats for as long as necessary.  It is performed using the ogo scale and in free rhythm.  Throughout, when possible, performers are to play rapid runs, alternate tension and repose and modulate frequently.  [B]Each chanter always does the main melody and should perform expressively.  [B]The Meadow of Playing has a well-defined multi-passage structure: three to five unrelated passages, a bridge-passage and a finale.  [B]Each of the simple passages gradually slows as it comes to an end, and it is to be very loud.  Each of the chanters' voices covers its entire range.  [B]The bridge-passage slows and broadens, and it is to be very soft.  Each of the chanters' voices stays in the high register.  [B]The finale is consistently slowing, and it is to become softer and softer.  Each of the chanters' voices stays in the high register.  [B]Scales are constructed from twenty-four notes spaced evenly throughout the octave.  The tonic note is a fixed tone passed from teacher to student.  [B]The ogo pentatonic scale is constructed by selection of degrees from the fundamental scale.  The degrees selected are the 1st, the 7th, the 12th, the 16th and the 20th.

The Satiny Phrases is a form of music used for entertainment originating in The Poison of Typhoons.  The rules of the form are applied by composers to produce individual pieces of music which can be performed.  One to two chanters recite nonsensical words and sounds while the music is played on a smal.  The musical voices bring melody with harmony.  The melody has phrases of varied length throughout the form.  It is performed using the asmuk scale and in free rhythm.  Throughout, when possible, composers and performers are to play legato.  [B]Each chanter always should be melancholic.  The voice ranges from the middle register to the high register.  [B]The smal always should perform with feeling.  [B]The Satiny Phrases has the following structure: a passage and an additional passage.  [B]The first simple passage is voiced by the melody of the smal.  The passage gradually slows as it comes to an end, and it is to be loud.  This passage features only melodic tones and intervals.  [B]The second simple passage is voiced by the melody of the chanters reciting a composition of The Wispy Luxuries and the harmony of the smal.  The passage is consistently slowing, and it is to become louder and louder.  Only one pitch is ever played at a time in this passage.  The passage should be composed and performed using locally improvisation.  The passage should sometimes include a falling-rising melody pattern, always include a falling melody pattern with sharpened sixth degree, sharpened third degree and sharpened fourth degree as well as glides, grace notes, mordents and rapid runs, always include a rising-falling melody pattern with glides, trills and arpeggios and always include a rising melody pattern with flattened fifth degree, flattened fourth degree and sharpened second degree as well as glides, mordents, arpeggios and staccato.  [B]Scales are constructed from twenty-four notes spaced evenly throughout the octave.  The tonic note is a fixed tone passed from teacher to student.  [B]The asmuk hexatonic scale is constructed by selection of degrees from the fundamental scale.  The degrees selected are the 1st, the 5th, the 10th, the 12th, the 17th and the 20th.

The Festive Mirth is a devotional form of music originating in The Poison of Typhoons.  The rules of the form are applied by composers to produce individual pieces of music which can be performed.  The music is played on a snosm.  The entire performance accelerates as it proceeds.  The melody has short phrases throughout the form.  Only one pitch is ever played at a time.  It is performed using the xenmu scale and in free rhythm.  Throughout, when possible, composers and performers are to use mordents, make trills and alternate tension and repose.  [B]The snosm always does the main melody and should sparkle.  [B]The Festive Mirth has a well-defined multi-passage structure: an introduction, a first theme, an exposition of the first theme, a lengthy bridge-passage, a second theme, a brief exposition of the second theme and a synthesis of previous passages.  [B]The introduction is to fade into silence.  [B]The first theme is to become louder and louder.  [B]The first exposition is to start loud then be immediately soft.  [B]The bridge-passage is to fade into silence.  [B]The second theme is to be moderately loud.  [B]The second exposition is to be very soft.  [B]The synthesis is to be loud.  [B]Scales are constructed from twenty-four notes spaced evenly throughout the octave.  The tonic note is a fixed tone passed from teacher to student.  [B]The xenmu hexatonic scale is constructed by selection of degrees from the fundamental scale.  The degrees selected are the 1st, the 6th, the 9th, the 15th, the 17th and the 21st.

The Beige Lace is a form of music used for entertainment originating in The Poison of Typhoons.  The rules of the form are applied by composers to produce individual pieces of music which can be performed.  The music is played on a stuk and three zos.  The music is melody and rhythm without harmony.  The melody has long phrases throughout the form.  Throughout, when possible, composers and performers are to make trills, alternate tension and repose and play staccato.  [B]The stuk always provides the rhythm and should feel mysterious.  [B]Each zos always does the main melody and should evoke tears.  [B]The Beige Lace has a well-defined multi-passage structure: a first theme, an exposition of the first theme, a bridge-passage, a second theme, a lengthy exposition of the second theme and a synthesis of previous passages.  [B]The first theme gradually slows as it comes to an end, and it is to be moderately soft.  Only one pitch is ever played at a time in this passage.  The passage is performed using the usnusp scale and in free rhythm.  [B]The first exposition is fast, and it is to be moderately soft.  Only one pitch is ever played at a time in this passage.  The passage is performed using the ekxox scale and in the odu rhythm.  [B]The bridge-passage is at a free tempo, and it is to be very soft.  This passage features only melodic tones and intervals.  The passage is performed using the abo scale and in the ozse rhythm.  [B]The second theme is extremely fast, and it is to fade into silence.  Only one pitch is ever played at a time in this passage.  The passage is performed without preference for a scale and in the usmdas rhythm.  [B]The second exposition is slow, and it is to start loud then be immediately soft.  Only one pitch is ever played at a time in this passage.  The passage is performed using the lâsm scale and in the ugas rhythm.  [B]The synthesis is consistently slowing, and it is to start loud then be immediately soft.  This passage features only melodic tones and intervals.  The passage is performed using the lûbu scale and in the gosma rhythm.  [B]Scales are constructed from twenty-four notes spaced evenly throughout the octave.  The tonic note is a fixed tone passed from teacher to student.  [B]The usnusp pentatonic scale is constructed by selection of degrees from the fundamental scale.  The degrees selected are the 1st, the 5th, the 12th, the 17th and the 21st.  [B]The ekxox pentatonic scale is constructed by selection of degrees from the fundamental scale.  The degrees selected are the 1st, the 7th, the 11th, the 14th and the 23rd.  [B]The abo hexatonic scale is constructed by selection of degrees from the fundamental scale.  The degrees selected are the 1st, the 5th, the 9th, the 12th, the 19th and the 21st.  [B]The lâsm heptatonic scale is constructed by selection of degrees from the fundamental scale.  The degrees selected are the 1st, the 4th, the 8th, the 9th, the 12th, the 14th and the 19th.  [B]The lûbu heptatonic scale is constructed by selection of degrees from the fundamental scale.  The degrees selected are the 1st, the 2nd, the 7th, the 10th, the 13th, the 16th and the 18th.  [B]The rhythm system is fundamentally polyrhythmic.  There are always multiple rhythm lines, and each of their bars is played over the same period of time, regardless of the number of beats.  The rhythm lines are thought of as one, without a primary-subordinate relationship, though individual lines can be named.  [B]The rhythm system is fundamentally polymetric.  There are always multiple rhythm lines, and the beats are always played together, even if one rhythm line completes (and then repeats) before the other is finished.  The rhythm lines are thought of as one, without a primary-subordinate relationship, though individual lines can be named.  [B]The odu rhythm is a single line with two beats.  The beats are named nuklat (spoken nu) and ost (ost).  The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| x x | [B]where x is a beat and | indicates a bar.  [B]The ozse rhythm is a single line with two beats.  The beats are named slusna (spoken slu) and sasne (sa).  The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| x - | [B]where x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar.  [B]The usmdas rhythm is a single line with eight beats divided into four bars in a 2-2-2-2 pattern.  The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| - x | x - | x x | x - | [B]where x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar.  [B]The ugas rhythm is made from two patterns: the urdu and the usmdas.  As stated above, they are to be played in polyrhythm.  [B]The urdu rhythm is a single line with four beats.  The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| x - x - | [B]where x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar.  [B]The gosma rhythm is made from two patterns: the urdu (considered the primary) and the ozse.  As stated above, they are to be played in polyrhythm.

The beats are named nol (spoken no), dab (da), agun (ag), ung (ung), stotho (sto), bor (bo), osm (osm) and enu (en). The Sweetnesses of Silkiness is a form of music used for entertainment originating in The Gale of Butterflies.  The form guides musicians during improvised performances.  A singer recites a composition of The Truth of Letters.  The melody has phrases of varied length throughout the form.  Only one pitch is ever played at a time.  It is performed using the cebela scale and in the cenopu rhythm.  Throughout, when possible, performers are to use mordents, alternate tension and repose and spread syllables over many notes.  [B]The singer always does the main melody and should feel mysterious.  [B]The Sweetnesses of Silkiness has a well-defined multi-passage structure: an introduction, a first theme, an exposition of the first theme, a lengthy bridge-passage, a second theme, an exposition of the second theme, a synthesis of previous passages and a finale.  [B]The introduction is very fast, and it is to be very soft.  The singer's voice ranges from the low register to the middle register.  [B]The first theme is consistently slowing, and it is to be very loud.  The singer's voice ranges from the middle register to the high register.  [B]The first exposition is extremely fast, and it is to be very soft.  The singer's voice covers its entire range.  [B]The bridge-passage is very fast, and it is to be soft.  The singer's voice stays in the middle register.  [B]The second theme gradually slows as it comes to an end, and it is to be very loud.  The singer's voice ranges from the middle register to the high register.  [B]The second exposition is very fast, and it is to be very loud.  The singer's voice stays in the high register.  [B]The synthesis is extremely fast, and it is to be moderately loud.  The singer's voice covers its entire range.  [B]The finale is at a free tempo, and it is to be moderately soft.  The singer's voice covers its entire range.  [B]Scales are conceived of as two chords built using a division of the perfect fourth interval into eleven notes.  The tonic note is fixed only at the time of performance.  [B]As always, the cebela hexatonic scale is thought of as two disjoint chords drawn from the fundamental division of the perfect fourth.  These chords are named ifife and fena.  [B]The ifife tetrachord is the 1st, the 3rd, the 6th and the 11th degrees of the fundamental perfect fourth division.  [B]The fena trichord is the 1st, the 4th and the 11th degrees of the fundamental perfect fourth division.  [B]The cenopu rhythm is a single line with three beats.  The beats are named èle (spoken èl), timafi (ti) and emu (em).  The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| x x - | [B]where x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar.

The Mauve Trumpets is a form of music used during marches and military engagements originating in The Gale of Butterflies.  The rules of the form are applied by composers to produce individual pieces of music which can be performed.  The music is played on a tafizè, a neli and a cani.  The musical voices join in melody, counterpoint and harmony.  The entire performance is extremely fast.  The melody has mid-length phrases, while the counterpoint has phrases of varied length throughout the form.  It is performed in the úpe rhythm.  Throughout, when possible, composers and performers are to alternate tension and repose.  [B]The tafizè always does the main melody and should be merry.  [B]The neli always does harmony and should perform sweetly.  [B]The cani always does the counterpoint melody and should be vigorous.  [B]The Mauve Trumpets has the following structure: one to two passages and an additional passage.  [B]Each of the first simple passages is to be moderately soft.  The tafizè ranges from the nasal low register to the strident middle register, the cani ranges from the sparkling low register to the wispy middle register and the neli stays in the crisp high register.  This passage typically has some sparse chords.  Each passage is performed using the lari scale.  [B]The second simple passage is to start loud then be immediately soft.  The tafizè ranges from the strident middle register to the harsh high register, the cani stays in the wispy middle register and the neli ranges from the heavy low register to the slicing middle register.  This passage features only melodic tones and intervals.  The passage is performed using the ÿaniye scale.  [B]Scales are conceived of as two chords built using a division of the perfect fourth interval into eleven notes.  The tonic note is fixed only at the time of performance.  [B]As always, the lari heptatonic scale is thought of as two disjoint chords drawn from the fundamental division of the perfect fourth.  These chords are named eyo and thili.  [B]The eyo tetrachord is the 1st, the 4th, the 8th and the 11th degrees of the fundamental perfect fourth division.  [B]The thili tetrachord is the 1st, the 5th, the 6th and the 11th degrees of the fundamental perfect fourth division.  [B]As always, the ÿaniye heptatonic scale is thought of as two disjoint chords drawn from the fundamental division of the perfect fourth.  These chords are named warerè and fathinu.  [B]The warerè tetrachord is the 1st, the 2nd, the 6th and the 11th degrees of the fundamental perfect fourth division.  [B]The fathinu tetrachord is the 1st, the 2nd, the 7th and the 11th degrees of the fundamental perfect fourth division.  [B]The úpe rhythm is a single line with eighteen beats divided into six bars in a 3-3-3-3-3-3 pattern.  The beats are named amama (spoken am), thafatha (tha) and etini (et).  The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| x - x | x X x | X x x | x x - | x - x | - x x | [B]where X marks an accented beat, x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar.

The Wisp of Sparkles is a form of music used to commemorate important events originating in The Gale of Butterflies.  The rules of the form are applied by composers to produce individual pieces of music which can be performed.  The music is played on a cani and three neli.  The music is melody and rhythm without harmony.  It is performed using the atho scale and in the opa rhythm.  Throughout, when possible, composers and performers are to play rapid runs.  [B]The cani always should feel mournful.  [B]Each neli always does the main melody and should bring a sense of motion.  [B]The Wisp of Sparkles has a well-defined multi-passage structure: a lengthy introduction and a lengthy verse and a chorus all repeated one to two times.  [B]The introduction is voiced by the melody of the cani and the melody of the neli.  The passage is extremely fast, and it is to be moderately loud.  The cani covers its entire range from the sparkling low register to the dark high register and each of the neli ranges from the heavy low register to the slicing middle register.  The passage has phrases of varied length in the melody.  This passage features only melodic tones and intervals.  [B]The verse is voiced by the melody of the neli and the rhythm of the cani.  The passage is fast, and it is to start loud then be immediately soft.  Each of the neli stays in the crisp high register and the cani ranges from the sparkling low register to the wispy middle register.  The passage has long phrases in the melody.  Chords are packed close together in dense clusters in this passage.  The passage should be composed and performed using mordents.  [B]The chorus is voiced by the melody of the cani and the melody of the neli.  The passage gradually slows as it comes to an end, and it is to be very soft.  The cani ranges from the sparkling low register to the wispy middle register and each of the neli stays in the crisp high register.  The passage has long phrases in the melody.  This passage is richly layered with full chords making use of the available range.  [B]Scales are conceived of as two chords built using a division of the perfect fourth interval into eleven notes.  The tonic note is fixed only at the time of performance.  [B]As always, the atho pentatonic scale is thought of as two disjoint chords drawn from the fundamental division of the perfect fourth.  These chords are named adi and aweme.  [B]The adi trichord is the 1st, the 3rd and the 11th degrees of the fundamental perfect fourth division.  [B]The aweme trichord is the 1st, the 5th and the 11th degrees of the fundamental perfect fourth division.  [B]The opa rhythm is made from three patterns: the dinade (considered the primary), the mafina and the pama.  The patterns are to be played over the same period of time, concluding together regardless of beat number.  [B]The dinade rhythm is a single line with four beats.  The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| - - - x | [B]where x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar.  [B]The mafina rhythm is a single line with ten beats divided into two bars in a 5-5 pattern.  The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| X x x - - | - x x - - | [B]where X marks an accented beat, x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar.  [B]The pama rhythm is a single line with thirty-two beats divided into four bars in a 8-8-8-8 pattern.  The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| x - - - - - - x | - x x x X x x x | - - x - - - - - | x x - x - - X - | [B]where X marks an accented beat, x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar.

The Droplet of Gloss is a devotional form of music originating in The Gale of Butterflies.  The form guides musicians during improvised performances.  The music is played on three tafizè and a etathu.  The music is melody and rhythm without harmony.  The entire performance should feel mournful and is moderately fast.  The melody has mid-length phrases throughout the form.  It is performed using the datome scale and in free rhythm.  Throughout, when possible, performers are to modulate frequently. [B]The chanter always should be passionate.  [B]The nakis always should perform expressively.  [B]The gumùr always should feel heroic.  [B]The Flute of Scintillating has a well-defined multi-passage structure: a brief theme, a brief bridge-passage and a lengthy series of variations on the theme possibly all repeated.  [B]The theme is voiced by the melody of the chanter and the counterpoint of the gumùr.  The chanter's voice stays in the middle register.  Only one pitch is ever played at a time in this passage.  [B]The bridge-passage is voiced by the melody of the chanter, the melody of the gumùr and the harmony of the nakis.  The chanter's voice ranges from the low register to the middle register and the nakis ranges from the piercing middle register to the dull high register.  This passage features only melodic tones and intervals.  [B]The series of variations is voiced by the melody of the nakis, the melody of the gumùr and the counterpoint of the chanter.  The nakis covers its entire range and the chanter's voice ranges from the low register to the middle register.  This passage features only melodic tones and intervals.  [B]Scales are constructed from twenty-four notes spaced evenly throughout the octave.  The tonic note is a fixed tone passed from teacher to student.  After a scale is constructed, notes are named according to degree.  The names are feb (spoken fe), berim (be), ibruk (ib), ermis (erm), thoth (tho), thatthil (tha) and gòstang (gò).  [B]The izeg hexatonic scale is thought of as two disjoint chords spanning a tritone and a perfect fourth.  These chords are named mabdug and sedil.  [B]The mabdug trichord is the 1st, the 12th and the 13th degrees of the quartertone octave scale.  [B]The sedil tetrachord is the 15th, the 19th, the 21st and the 25th (completing the octave) degrees of the quartertone octave scale.
